title: Fix conformance test fixture path assumption (broken standalone)
description: tests/ConformanceTest.php (as committed on origin/main) loads fixtures via __DIR__ . '/../../../../tests/sdk-conformance/cases.json', a path that only resolves if this repo is checked out as a subdirectory of a pdftract monorepo. In the actual standalone pdftract-php repo that directory does not exist, so setUp() calls $this->fail(...) immediately -- every test in the shipped suite fails before it can run. Fix by vendoring the conformance fixtures into this repo (e.g. tests/fixtures/) or fetching them from the pdftract project's release artifacts, and update the path constants accordingly. See docs/plan/plan.md (Known issues) for context. Verify with: composer install && ./vendor/bin/phpunit

title: Client extract/text/markdown/stream/metadata methods construct CLI args that fail against the real pdftract binary
description:
Direct testing against a real built pdftract binary (upstream pdftract repo, release build) shows that most of src/Pdftract/Client.php's methods are NOT just undocumented or duplicated-boilerplate (see bf-5g9) but are syntactically broken and cannot succeed at all, contradicting docs/plan/plan.md's framing that "the Client works by shelling out to a local pdftract binary."

Root cause: extract(), extractText(), extractMarkdown(), extractStream(), and getMetadata() all omit the required "extract" subcommand token that pdftract's clap CLI expects as the first argument (Commands::Extract in the upstream pdftract repo's crates/pdftract-cli/src/cli.rs). Confirmed by running the exact argv each method builds:

- extract(path) builds argv [path] -> error: unrecognized subcommand for the path itself
- extractText(path) builds argv [--text, path] -> error: unexpected argument --text found
- extractMarkdown(path) builds argv [--md, path] -> error: unexpected argument --md found
- extractStream(path) builds argv [path] -> same unrecognized-subcommand error as extract()
- getMetadata(path) builds argv [--metadata-only, path] -> error: unexpected argument --metadata-only found

Even after prepending "extract", two more bugs remain:
- extractText()/extractMarkdown() must pass an explicit output target after --text/--md (clap's --text/--md take a PATH value, e.g. a dash for stdout: extract --text <dash> <input>); passing the bare input path right after --text/--md causes clap to consume it as --text's value and then fail with "the following required arguments were not provided: INPUT" (reproduced).
- getMetadata()'s --metadata-only flag does not exist anywhere in the current pdftract CLI at all (confirmed: extract --metadata-only <file> fails with "unexpected argument --metadata-only found, tip: a similar argument exists: --md"), independent of subcommand placement. This SDK method cannot be fixed by argument-ordering alone; either upstream pdftract needs to restore/add a metadata-only mode, or getMetadata() needs reimplementing on top of a real flag (e.g. extract --json <dash-for-stdout>, filtered client-side for just the metadata block).

verifyReceipt(path, receipt) also has a semantic mismatch: it passes the receipt string as the bare second positional, which pdftract's VerifyReceiptCommand (upstream repo's crates/pdftract-cli/src/verify_receipt.rs) treats as a receipt file PATH, not inline content -- inline receipt strings require a separate --inline flag. Reproduced: passing an inline string produces "Error: Failed to read receipt from ..." because the CLI tried to read it as a path.

Only hash() is confirmed fully correct and working end-to-end (pdftract hash <file> returns a real fingerprint). classify() has correct CLI form (pdftract classify <file> parses fine) but the binary tested here was built without the "profiles" Cargo feature (pdftract's default feature set is empty in crates/pdftract-cli/Cargo.toml), so it errors at runtime needing that feature. search() similarly requires the non-default "grep" feature; the binary tested here doesn't have it, producing an unrecognized-subcommand error for grep -- verify against a feature-complete build before assuming search()'s argument construction is otherwise correct.

For comparison, the sibling pdftract-go SDK in the upstream monorepo (pdftract-go/pdftract.go) gets this right: its Extract-family methods all prepend the "extract" subcommand before --json/--text/--metadata-only etc. It also assumes the now-nonexistent --metadata-only flag, suggesting that flag was removed or renamed upstream after all SDKs were written and no SDK (php or go) has been updated since.

This bug affects the CURRENTLY COMMITTED, shipped src/Pdftract/Client.php on origin/main -- it is not part of the uncommitted ADR-1 HTTP-migration WIP (bf-4gq) and is independent of it (the same argument-construction bugs would need fixing in the HTTP request-building code too, if/when that lands, since the HTTP handlers wrap similar option semantics). It's also relevant to bf-5g9 (dedupe proc_open blocks) -- that bead currently says "keep behavior identical, this is a pure refactor," which would just relocate/preserve these bugs into a refactored shared method rather than fix them; the two should probably be done together, or this one done first.

Verify a fix by building pdftract with default (empty) features, matching a typical release build, then running each Client method against a small fixture PDF under tests/sdk-conformance/fixtures/ and confirming real output instead of a CLI parse error.

title: Add batch/concurrent extraction API once ADR-1 HTTP client lands
description: Once the ADR-1 HTTP-client migration (docs/plan/plan.md) is in place, add a Client::extractBatch(array $sources, array $options = []): array method that fires concurrent HTTP requests (e.g. via curl_multi) instead of forcing callers to loop and await one extract() at a time. This is the kind of batch PDF-processing workload the CLI-subprocess design could never support well (one OS process per call); it becomes cheap once the transport is HTTP. Depends on the HTTP client migration bead landing first -- do not start until Client has a working HTTP transport.

title: OPS-GATED: ADR-1 assumes pdftract --serve covers all 9 SDK methods; only 3 have HTTP routes today
description:
docs/plan/plan.md's ADR-1 (2026-07-20) decides: "pdftract-php will become an HTTP client against pdftract --serve, replacing the proc_open subprocess wrapper as the SDK's sole transport" -- covering all 9 documented Client methods (extract, extractText, extractMarkdown, extractStream, search, getMetadata, hash, classify, verifyReceipt).

Checked against the upstream pdftract repo's actual serve-mode implementation (crates/pdftract-cli/src/serve.rs): the HTTP server currently exposes exactly 5 routes -- root, POST /extract, POST /extract/text, POST /extract/stream, and GET /health. That covers only 3 of the 9 SDK methods (extract, extractText, extractStream). There is no HTTP route at all for:

- search() -- no equivalent of the CLI's grep subcommand
- getMetadata() -- no lightweight metadata-only endpoint (would have to reuse the full /extract response)
- hash() -- no equivalent of the CLI's hash subcommand
- classify() -- no equivalent of the CLI's classify subcommand
- verifyReceipt() -- no equivalent of the CLI's verify-receipt subcommand
- extractMarkdown() -- no dedicated route; markdown output is controlled by a markdown_anchors flag on /extract or /extract/text, not confirmed equivalent to the CLI's --md output

Additionally, no OpenAPI/schema description of the serve API exists anywhere in the upstream repo (no file matching *openapi* was found, and the serve module doesn't use an OpenAPI-generation crate), even though ADR-1's plan explicitly calls for regenerating/auditing the SDK's Models/Codegen tree "against the actual HTTP OpenAPI schema pdftract --serve exposes" -- that schema does not exist yet to regenerate against.

This means ADR-1's "sole transport" framing is currently unachievable for 6 of 9 methods without new upstream work in the pdftract repo itself (adding routes for search, hash, classify, verifyReceipt, getMetadata, and ideally publishing an OpenAPI schema for serve). bf-4gq (reconcile the WIP per ADR-1) does not currently call this out, and could otherwise proceed as if HTTP parity were just a client-side implementation task.

This needs a human decision, not just engineering follow-through, since it changes the shape of ADR-1 itself. Options to weigh: (a) coordinate/track the upstream serve-mode route additions as a prerequisite, (b) keep a CLI-subprocess fallback specifically for the methods HTTP can't reach yet (revisits ADR-1's rejected "support both transports" alternative, at least partially and temporarily), or (c) drop those methods from pdftract-php's v1 HTTP-only surface and re-add them once upstream catches up. Whoever picks this up should re-read ADR-1 in full and decide which of these (or another option) to adopt before bf-4gq's implementation proceeds past the 3 methods serve-mode already supports.

title: Reconcile abandoned working-tree WIP per ADR-1 (HTTP client migration)
description: The lab checkout has ~7 weeks of uncommitted, half-finished work (src/Client.php, src/Codegen/, src/Models/ at the src/ root, plus modified composer.json/README.md/phpunit.xml/tests/ConformanceTest.php) that starts migrating the SDK from a proc_open CLI-subprocess wrapper to an HTTP client, but only reimplements 2 of 25 model classes and leaves a stub Codegen/Methods.php ('This class will be populated with auto-generated methods'). docs/plan/plan.md ADR-1 (2026-07-20) decides the SDK should move to an HTTP client against 'pdftract --serve'. This bead is to execute that decision: finish the HTTP Client implementation, port the remaining model classes and the full exception hierarchy, delete the superseded src/Pdftract/ tree once nothing references it, and fix the composer.json PSR-4 autoload root consistently (src/ vs src/Pdftract/ -- currently the committed and uncommitted trees disagree). Read docs/plan/plan.md ADR-1 in full before starting.

title: Dedupe six proc_open/pipe-handling blocks in src/Pdftract/Client.php
description: In the committed Client.php (src/Pdftract/Client.php), extractText(), extractMarkdown(), extractStream(), search(), and verifyReceipt() each hand-roll their own ~30-line proc_open/escapeshellcmd/pipe-reading block instead of reusing the private exec() helper that extract(), getMetadata(), hash(), and classify() already share. Refactor all methods to go through one shared private transport method (extend exec() to optionally return raw stdout or a streaming generator instead of only decoded JSON). This is useful even independent of the ADR-1 HTTP migration since it's the code as currently shipped on origin/main. Keep behavior identical -- this is a pure refactor, add/extend phpunit coverage to pin current behavior before refactoring.

comments.author: cli
comments.text: Heads up before treating this as a pure behavior-preserving refactor: bf-1s2 documents that most of these proc_open methods (extract, extractText, extractMarkdown, extractStream, getMetadata) are already syntactically broken against the real pdftract CLI (missing the extract subcommand token, and getMetadata using a --metadata-only flag that does not exist upstream). Only hash() is confirmed working. Read bf-1s2 first -- deduping should fix the argument construction, not just relocate the existing bugs into a shared helper.

title: Add CI workflow for pdftract-php (phpunit + composer validate)
description: pdftract-php has no CI configured anywhere -- no workflow files in the repo, and no entry for it in the fleet's Argo WorkflowTemplate table (jedarden/declarative-config k8s/iad-ci/argo-workflows/). This is why the broken conformance-suite fixture path (see the 'Fix conformance test fixture path assumption' bead) went unnoticed. Add a WorkflowTemplate (e.g. pdftract-php-ci) to jedarden/declarative-config following the pattern of forge-ci/needle-ci, triggered on push to jedarden/pdftract-php (Forgejo, git.ardenone.com), running composer validate, composer install, and ./vendor/bin/phpunit. Add it to the WorkflowTemplate table in this workspace's CLAUDE.md once live.

title: Publish jedarden/pdftract on Packagist or fix install instructions
description: README.md instructs 'composer require jedarden/pdftract' but the package is not listed on Packagist (confirmed via search 2026-07-20), so that command fails for any external user with a stock Composer config. Either submit the package to Packagist (packagist.org, requires a stable tagged release and probably the ADR-1 HTTP-client migration + fixed conformance suite landing first so v1.0.0 is something worth publishing) or, in the interim, update README.md's Installation section to the working VCS-repository incantation (composer.json repositories entry pointing at git.ardenone.com/jedarden/pdftract-php) so the documented install path actually works today.

title: Add timeout to Client subprocess/HTTP calls (currently unbounded)
description: No proc_open() call in src/Pdftract/Client.php sets a timeout. A hung or pathologically slow pdftract invocation (e.g. a malformed/huge PDF) blocks the calling PHP process indefinitely, with no way for a caller to bound it. Add a constructor-configurable timeout (e.g. $timeoutSeconds, default a few seconds for metadata/hash, longer for extract/OCR) enforced via stream_select()/proc_terminate() on the child process. If ADR-1's HTTP migration (see docs/plan/plan.md) lands first, apply the equivalent as a curl CURLOPT_TIMEOUT / connect-timeout instead -- whichever transport is current when this is picked up.
